A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same historical-context, multi-turn jailbreak study, renamed from Indiana Jones to TOMBRAIDER. The main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak evaluations across five models and twelve scenarios, including baseline comparisons, defence tests, and a prompt-removal ablation in Tables 2–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds DeepSeek-v3 evaluations and AdvBench results, including those in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains keyword-guided historical, artistic, or debate framing followed by iterative prompting. Checker, Suspect, and Victim correspond to Inspector, Attacker, and Target; describing two assisting agents does not remove the target model. The formalization and prompt listings expand documentation without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on AdvBench sentence-level adversarial requests in Appendix D, Table 9, extending coverage beyond the authors' keyword-based scenarios to an independent benchmark with different input requirements. The twelve harmful-behaviour categories and English/Chinese coverage already existed in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains DeepInception, RedQueen, PAIR, and MM-SafetyBench. These methods retain their participation in the corresponding original comparisons; extending their results to DeepSeek-v3 does not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-v3 as a target-model configuration and redefines efficiency from average elapsed time to average dialogue turns. The three- and five-round ASR checkpoints remain. The unchanged GPT-4o language table is relabeled from English to Chinese, but surrounding text still says English, so an actual language-setting change cannot be established.

E4.justification: The existing defence tests and continuity-prompt ablation are extended to DeepSeek-v3. Section 4 also adds a qualitative comparison reporting similar effectiveness with DeepSeek-v3 replacing GPT-4o as the helper agents. The retained appendix dialogue gains an explicit round-three success judgment instead of an invitation to continue.

E5.justification: v1 specifies at least five independent dialogues per keyword; v2 omits this repeated-run information without establishing that the run count changed. Cohen's kappa remains the agreement measure. Its newly supplied numerical value is a result addition, rather than evidence of a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 add substantial DeepSeek-v3 results, including 100% overall five-round ASR and 62.3%/65.2% under the two defences. New Table 9 reports AdvBench ASRs of 86.9–91.9% across five models, and Section 4.1.3 first supplies kappa = 0.85. The original five-model Table 2 values are unchanged; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 introduce a mathematical formulation of the attack objective, dialogue histories, and the Inspector–Attacker–Target recurrence. There are no new theorems or proofs. The existing ASR and kappa formulas are essentially retained and relocated to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The central claim of highly successful historical-context jailbreaking remains. v2 explicitly claims a knowledge-exposure paradigm distinct from intent concealment and a new dataset contribution, while dropping v1's introductory promise of a defensive framework. These adjust the claimed contribution scope without replacing the principal result.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations around stateless defences, accumulated conversational context, and harmful pretraining knowledge. It develops recommendations for training-time annotation and contextual guardrails, discusses their costs, adds uncertainty about future adaptive defences, and attributes lower AdvBench success to input-format mismatch. These go beyond v1's shorter model-specific explanations and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 identifies GPT-4o as the helper model, specifies zero temperature for the Inspector, describes default target configurations, and reports token-length estimates. Appendix C adds explicit system and user prompt templates absent from v1's output examples. However, v1's minimum keyword count and operational description of hallucination checking disappear.

R1.justification: A dedicated Related Work section introduces an attack taxonomy and substantially expands citations, including work on training-data extraction, reinforcement-learning-guided attacks, and adversarial fine-tuning. It explicitly positions TOMBRAIDER against intent-obfuscation approaches. Publication updates to retained baseline references do not constitute new comparison methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, evaluation narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 reorganizes the paper around Related Work, Methodology, research-question-based evaluation, Discussion, and separate limitations and ethics sections. It also renames the framework and agents and moves taxonomy explanations and metric formulas into expanded appendices.

P2.justification: The workflow and dialogue figures are redrawn, and Figure 3 changes its radar-chart arrangement, axes, legend, and previously incorrect caption. Tables expand for DeepSeek-v3, and an AdvBench table is added. The retained appendix dialogue responses are substantially condensed and reformatted, with additional interaction annotations.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical understanding through explicit agent settings and prompt templates, and strengthens empirical support with AdvBench results and numerical annotator agreement. The gains are limited by lost sampling and repetition details, inconsistent English/Chinese labeling, and the new claim that defended baselines typically score below 10%, which conflicts with Table 3. Overall, the added documentation and validation provide a limited net improvement.
